newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ABN AMRO TO INVEST $100 MLN IN HUNGARY'S MHB.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO TO INVEST $100 MLN IN HUNGARY'S MHB.

text.p: ABN AMRO NV said on Friday that in addition to buying an 89.23 percent stake in Hungary's Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB) for $89.23 million it would invest another $100 million dollars in the next 12 months.
"In addition to the purchase price ABN AMRO will invest another 100 million dollars in MHB over the next year," Michael J Drabbe, head of ABN AMRO International, told reporters in Budapest.
"We aim to become one of the top three banks in the central and east European region (and) our new acquisistion will enhance this position enormously."
Hungary's finance ministry confirmed on Friday that Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV had been chosen to take over the bank.
"The finance ministry's decision was to sell an 89 percent stake to ABN AMRO," said Agnes Balazs deputy state secretary at the finance ministry.
"The purchase price means that the 89 percent share package of MHB was sold at 222 percent of the shares' nominal value," Balazs added.

The official announcement came after a meeting of Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt on Wednesday chose ABN AMRO over Austria's Creditanstalt-Bankverein but declined to make the decision public until the finance ministry's offical announcement on Friday.
ABN Amro and Creditanstalt both had submitted bids in the one-round tender for the sale of an 89.23 percent stake.

MHB is Hungary's fifth largest commercial bank with a network of 70 branches across the country. It is also a leading bank for domestic major companies and is active in capital markets, leasing and factoring.
MHB has plans to regroup 40 of its branches in retail banking under a subsidiary called MHB Nepbank, and would have 30 branches specialising in corporate clients.
"ABN AMRO fully underwrites the MHB boards development plans," Drabbe said.
In October, MHB said it has posted an after-tax profit of 3.44 billion forints for the first eight months of 1996, compared with 1.4 billion after-tax profits for all of 1995.

Under the leadership of its chief executive officer Zsigmond Jarai, who took over at MHB in 1995, the bank has written off millions of dollars of bad debt, cut staff by 40 percent to 2,500 and reduced operating costs.
